transfers.source_mechanism: Structured surface with hydrophilic and hydrophobic regions enables droplet nucleation, growth, and directional transport under specific environmental conditions
transfers.target_problem: Arid coastal regions experience regular fog events but almost no rain. Passive dew condensers using flat foil sheets achieve only 0.1-0.3 L/m²/night. A better surface design is needed that promotes dropwise condensation, nucleates droplets efficiently, transports them to drainage rapidly, is durable, low-cost, and requires no energy input.
transfers.transferred_principle: Hierarchical surface structure with differential wettability enables directional transport of condensed water droplets from atmosphere to collection point
transfers.required_translation: Replace insect exoskeleton material with food-grade polymer substrate; maintain microstructured hydrophilic/hydrophobic pattern using laser ablation or nanoimprint lithography; incorporate structural support for durability; design collection channel system that maintains gradient without energy input
transfers.expected_effect: Enhanced water collection rate through efficient nucleation, rapid droplet growth, and directional transport toward collection point
boundary_conditions: wind speeds that don't disrupt droplet growth (0.5-5 m/s)
failure_conditions: high wind speeds disrupting droplet transport
transfers.testable_prediction: A condenser surface with microstructured hydrophilic/hydrophobic pattern will collect at least 1.0 L/m²/night in fog conditions with 70-90% relative humidity at 10-20°C, compared to 0.1-0.3 L/m²/night for flat surfaces under identical conditions
